rows.headline: Alcantara over a collapsing Manaea at home, but Miami's thin pen and LH lineup keep it a coin flip
rows.analysis: Confirmed: Sandy Alcantara (RHP) vs Sean Manaea (LHP), Tue Sept 8, 6:40 pm ET at loanDepot park; books Miami -135 / Mets +116, flat since open (-134). Manaea is the lever: four straight starts of 4+ ER (7.23 ERA, 1.52 WHIP over 23.2 IP), 8.65 September ERA, fastball 91.3 mph, xERA 4.95, and a brutal times-through-order curve (2.94 ERA first time, 5.36 second, 7.36 third), so his outing is a 4-5 inning affair and the Mets' interim manager is openly weighing a bullpen move. Alcantara is a clear upgrade on paper (97.6 mph, 2.35 BB/9) but has lost four straight (12 ER in 25 IP) and his 4.28 xFIP says he is closer to average than his ERA. Two things cut against Miami: their lineup ran six left-handed bats Monday (Stowers, Conine, Caissie, Marsee, Pauley, Mack) against a lefty whose damage comes from RHB (.278/16 HR vs .245/5 HR), and their pen is depleted — Fairbanks (IL, back Wednesday at best), Bender and Nardi out, Ekness and Gibson on back-to-back days, Blalock 48 pitches Monday. The Mets' pen is healthier despite Williams and Perez on the IL: Senga is 6-for-6 closing and only Devenski is likely down. The Mets' lineup is also the better one and is hot. Net: home field plus the starter gap gives Miami a hair, nothing more, and nothing here is unpriced enough for a medal.

Books moved from -147 open to -170/-185 even after the lineup news, so sharp money is on LA. Plate umpire Cory Blaser runs a low-scoring game (8.09 R/G), neutral.
